title: Climbing Stairs
statement: You can climb 1 or 2 steps at a time. Return how many distinct ways you can climb to the top of `n` stairs.

predict_steps.prompt: What is dp[i] in terms of earlier cells?
predict_steps.hint: Last step was a 1-jump or a 2-jump.

viva.question: Why is climbing stairs a linear DP instead of an exponential recursion tree?
expected_points: each step i is computed once from the prior two answers
overlapping subproblems are reused instead of recomputed
total time is linear in the number of stairs
naive recursion rebranches into the same smaller heights many times

viva.question: What are the base answers for one and two stairs?
expected_points: one stair has exactly one way
two stairs have exactly two ways
without them the relation has nothing to build on

viva.question: Why does the recurrence add the previous two states?
expected_points: the final move is either a single step or a double step
those cases partition all legal paths
paths ending in a single step come from i-1
paths ending in a double step come from i-2
